conceptTour.title: Book One, concept by concept

scenes.name: The struggle
scenes.title: “Work hard, play by the rules, and you will get ahead.”
scenes.note: Distress is individualized while the architecture producing it is preserved.
scenes.source: The American Millennial Manifesto · Chapter Two
scenes.description: A person stands at the centre while six cultural messages press in: Your worth is what you earn. Do not risk your place. If it pays, it must be progress. Protect what is yours. Everyone does it. You have no choice. Rings of pain pulse outward from the person.

scenes.name: The cultural trap
scenes.title: “How we do things” begins to feel identical to “how things are.”
scenes.note: The Western civilization many of us inherited is neither sacred nor identical to reality. It is a historical Painting.
scenes.source: Book One · Architecture of Continuity · The Painting
scenes.description: The view pulls back as a ring closes around the whole scene and locks: a cultural trap. Around the trap: time as money, attention as inventory, nature as raw material, human beings as units of production.

scenes.name: The setup
scenes.title: Frames turn continuity into curriculum.
scenes.note: Learning requires enough stability for actions to have legible consequences and enough freedom for more than one response to remain possible.
scenes.source: Book One · Architecture of Continuity · Reality Frames
scenes.description: The trap turns out to be one of several cultures inside a larger ruled frame, RF₀, marked stable rules, legible consequences, and more than one response.

scenes.name: The turn
scenes.title: Understand what shapes you.
scenes.description: The lock springs open, the trap opens, and the person rises out through the opening.

interludes.name: The human character
interludes.title: Ego defends the Character Little c has learned to call itself.
interludes.note: In DOT’s account, Ego protects a familiar self-image. When that defence hardens into Arrogance, unfamiliar experience is more easily dismissed.
interludes.description: Little c remains distinct from the Canvas. On it, a painted body outline represents a protective self-image. As the outline hardens, a gate turns unfamiliar input away: an illustration of patterns in the Painting, not the location of the experiencer.

closing.title: Become a student of your own experience.

trailer.title: Digital Organism Theory
trailer.subtitle: A school of thought for examining experience.
trailer.note: The opening of the film: twelve shots, one idea each. Its words come from Book One, The American Millennial Manifesto, and the author; DOT’s proposals are labelled.

shots.label: The performance of normality
shots.description: One line draws a person. Around them an ordinary day repeats, a light circling faster each time: a laptop, a growing stack of bills, a phone with a feed moving up its screen, and a ranked row of people on rising bars. The person starts to smile, while rings of stress pulse at the chest behind the smile and the day presses closer.
lines: We go to work. We pay bills. We scroll. We compete.
We call exhaustion adulthood, anxiety responsibility,
isolation independence, and endless accumulation success.

shots.label: The picture
shots.description: Illustration from The American Millennial Manifesto: a flag-patterned cow, the Host, standing on cracked earth with a two-headed leech on its back, faces a phone-shaped mirror showing a healthy version of itself in a green meadow.
lines: We pretend the picture is coherent.

shots.label: People struggling
shots.description: Illustration from The American Millennial Manifesto: the Host rests its head beside a laptop at a kitchen table, carrying the leech. A meal sits untouched among household envelopes and keys, beside a picture of a cow in a green meadow.
lines: The body tightens. Attention fragments.
Trust declines. Meaning thins.

shots.label: The blame
shots.description: Illustration from The American Millennial Manifesto: the Host’s body opened like a butcher’s chart: labor and time, attention and data, savings and taxes, debt. Its head is labelled beliefs, identity, perception.
lines: The citizen is blamed. The architecture remains.

shots.label: What we are not taught
shots.description: One person stands in a measuring box. The view pulls far back to a lattice of boxed figures, each with a ring of stress, tugged on strings from the hand of a figure above who is boxed too. A soft light stays on the one person as six cultural messages drift in and settle around them: Your worth is what you earn. Do not risk your place. If it pays, it must be progress. Protect what is yours. Everyone does it. You have no choice.
lines: A society may generate enormous wealth
and still fail to teach people how to confront fear,
govern attention, inspect inherited identity,
or distinguish freedom from consumption.

shots.label: Power unanswered
shots.description: The view moves in on the one person. They look up to the figure above that holds their string, boxed and stressed too. That figure points back down at the person’s chest. The view pulls out: the lids press down, the boxes thicken, and every figure across the lattice dims and shrinks.
lines: A public can lose the habit
of requiring power to answer for its conduct
while continuing to describe itself as free.

shots.label: Moral erosion
shots.description: Illustration from The American Millennial Manifesto: the Host eats from a rusted trough labelled Moral Erosion, filled with phones, money, status, and fast food.
lines: Without a truthful framework, morality erodes.

shots.label: The question
shots.description: Everything clears. The person stands alone, and a heartbeat glows at the chest.
lines: So where does a truthful framework begin?
The most immediate fact of your existence
is not a measurement.
It is that you are here to experience one.

shots.label: DOT’s proposal
shots.description: The view pulls back: the living Avatar is distinct from Little c. A calm broken loop marks continuing process. Intent travels toward the body and experience returns through the embodied connection.
lines: You are Little c.
Your living body is your interface to a Reality Frame.

shots.label: The architecture
shots.description: The view pulls back from Little c to the Avatars in RF₀, an experience laboratory for Little cs. RF₀’s boundary and its Avatars light up, then its Reality Stream travels toward Little c. RF₀ and Little c are both within Big C, with Little c outside RF₀ and receiving its Reality Stream. Beyond Big C, T × E is labelled Speculation: its proposed preexisting conditions.
lines: RF₀ is an experience laboratory for Little cs.

shots.label: The opening
shots.description: The crowd grows still around the person. A jade light at the chest marks renewed attention to experience. The box dissolves, and paths open out from the person in every direction, each ending in an open choice.
lines: Conditioning is real. Conditioning is not essence.
What matters is what Little c does with the opening.
Freedom is participation in the creation of possibility.

shots.label: Digital Organism Theory
shots.description: The architecture rises above the title: Digital Organism Theory. A school of thought for examining experience.

screeningFilms.title: You, the Observer, Belong in the Inquiry
screeningFilms.summary: A personal introduction to Book One through familiar moments: a short message, learning a skill, and the marks experience leaves behind. Explore the Canvas, the Painting, Fear, Love, and the possibility of a different response. DOT’s larger claims about consciousness and physical reality remain hypotheses to test.

acts.title: Start with an ordinary moment
acts.summary: Begin with a familiar moment: a one-word reply can carry more than one meaning. The feeling is real; understanding it takes questions, comparison, and a willingness to revise.

acts.title: Explore the model
acts.summary: Explore DOT’s proposed architecture: Big C emerged within T × E (Speculation): T is primordial continuity—Time; E is the raw information source. The model’s starting assumptions invite prediction, evidence, and correction.

acts.title: Notice what experience leaves behind
acts.summary: Learning a skill changes what you can do even after practice ends. Explore the Canvas as what carries change forward, and the Painting as the patterns through which you meet the next moment.

acts.title: Make room for a different response
acts.summary: Notice when an old defense shapes a new conversation. In DOT, Love names the condition in which Fear no longer governs you, making room for truth, care, boundaries, and a different response.
